01 / THE CONCEPT

CAP -
Catch a Pervert

Camera-equipped smart glasses make recording strangers effortless. I wanted to give the people around them a say.

There’s very little room to consent, or even notice a camera, when it looks like an ordinary pair of glasses. CAP is my response to that imbalance, built through Critical Making & Tactical Media.

I use Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) advertisements to look for smart-glasses identifiers. Cappy turns a matching signal into an expressive face and a buzz you can feel, so you can decide how to respond.

I’m looking for the presence of camera wearables; a Bluetooth match doesn’t tell me whether their camera is recording.

WAYS TO WEAR

Wear Cappy your way

I designed around user freedom. How visible you want to be is up to you.

OUT IN THE OPEN

On your shirt

Let people meet Cappy. His reactions can start a conversation about recording, consent, and the person behind the lens.

JUST BETWEEN YOU TWO

On your waistband

Clip him discreetly to your pants and feel the vibration alerts privately. You choose whether to confront an onlooker.

DISTANCEFar

Quiet

When the coast is clear, Cappy gets some rest.

Cappy is already awake.

I’ve recreated Cappy’s reactions here so you can try them in your browser. Distance is simulated; his movement and the buzz text show the haptic patterns.

  1. HAPPY

    The coast is clear

    His default state: white eyes looking around, with no alerts to worry about.

    No buzz
  2. CURIOUS

    Something nearby

    A matching BLE signal catches his attention. His eyes turn yellow.

    Single sharp bzz
  3. ANGRY

    Getting too close

    Someone wearing smart glasses is getting closer. Red eyes make his objection clear.

    Double bzz-bzz
  4. RAGE

    Personal space, please

    They’ve ignored the warning and moved right in. His screen flashes red.

    Triple buzz
  5. SLEEPY

    Time for a nap

    After 30 seconds of quiet he gets sleepy; at 60 he’s asleep, zzZ. Double-knock his body to wake him, a little groggy.

    Double-knock to wake

Drag to rotate · + / − to zoom · Scroll the page to explore each part

01

THE ENCLOSURE

A squircle around a circle

I designed Cappy’s orange shell in Fusion 360. The two 3D-printed halves snap together around internal screen supports, with a dedicated slot for the on/off switch and access to the USB-C port.

3D-PRINTED SHELL · SNAP-FIT · USB-C ACCESS

02

THE DISPLAY

Cappy’s expressive face

I use a 1.28-inch round TFT LCD to give Cappy his eyes. LovyanGFX renders the blinks, glances, and state changes at around 30 frames per second, making the face feel alive between alerts.

GC9A01 · 240 × 240 PX · SPI · 30 FPS

Try his expressions ↑
03

THE BRAIN

Listening for smart glasses

The compact ESP32-S3-Zero runs continuous NimBLE advertisement scans. I match manufacturer IDs and device names, then smooth the RSSI readings to move Cappy through his proximity tiers without flickering between states.

ESP32-S3-ZERO · NimBLE · SMOOTHED RSSI

Inside Cappy’s firmware ↗
04

KNOCKS & BUZZES

Alerts you can feel

I configured the ADXL345 accelerometer as a physical knock detector: two knocks wake Cappy from a nap. A MOSFET-driven vibration motor gives single, double, or triple buzzes as the alert escalates, so you can respond without looking at his face.

ADXL345 · DOUBLE-KNOCK · MOSFET MOTOR DRIVER

━━ ━━ ━ ━
05

BATTERY & CHARGING

Ready to come along

A 3.7V LiPo battery and TP4056 USB-C charging circuit power the wearable. I soldered the connections into a self-contained unit, with a physical switch on the side to turn Cappy on and off.

3.7V LiPo · TP4056 · USB-C · ON/OFF SWITCH

04 / IN THE WILD

Cappy, out in the world

I gave the finished orange Cappy the photoshoot he deserved, then wore him into my final presentation.

ON YOUR WAISTBAND

A companion you can keep close

I also tried Cappy on my waistband. With the screen tucked under a shirt, his vibration alerts can stay between us. The same object lets you choose how much attention you want to draw.

YOUR PRIVACY. YOUR CALL.

MY FINAL POSTER & CLASS DEMO

MEETCAPPY

I kept the poster light on text and let Cappy’s personality take the lead: he looks around, gets angry for you, and rests when you’re safe.

For the live class demo, Sudarsini wore our improvised “unreleased” glasses while a test device triggered Cappy’s BLE detection. I showed his changing expressions, vibration alerts, and double-knock wake interaction on stage.
